articles.excerpt: I build MakeQuickWork, a small set of free browser tools, on my own. This post is about the Resize Image tool and the three things that took longer than the resize itself. Resizing an image in the bro…
articles.body: I build MakeQuickWork, a small set of free browser tools, on my own. This post is about the Resize Image tool and the three things that took longer than the resize itself. Resizing an image in the browser looks like one call: draw the image onto a smaller canvas with drawImage . That works, and on a big photo it also looks bad. The edges go jagged and fine texture turns into noise. Getting it to look right took one loop. Most of the rest of the time went into the size fields: what "keep aspect ratio" should mean when someone enters both a width and a height, and how big a canvas a phone will actually agree to create. The tool is here: https://makequickwork.com/image/resize-image/ . Everything runs in the tab.

articles.body: AWS CloudTrail What it is CloudTrail is an auditing and governance service that records API calls and account activity across your AWS account. Every time someone (or something) interacts with AWS, whether through the Console, CLI, SDK, or another AWS service, CloudTrail can log it. What each event records Who made the call (IAM user, role, root, or AWS service) What action was performed (e.g., RunInstances , DeleteBucket , PutObject ) When it happened (timestamp) Where it came from (source IP address, user agent) Which resources were affected Result (success or error code) Types of events Event type What it covers Logged by default?

articles.title: 26 of 114 sitemaps gave every URL the same lastmod. One repeated a millisecond 312 times.
articles.excerpt: I read 30,353 entries out of 114 sitemaps. On 26 of those domains, every single URL carried the same value. One domain repeated an identical timestamp — down to the millisecond — 312 times. That is no…
articles.body: I read 30,353 <loc> entries out of 114 sitemaps. On 26 of those domains, every single URL carried the same <lastmod> value. One domain repeated an identical timestamp — down to the millisecond — 312 times. That is not a freshness signal. That is a build log line that wandered into an XML file. Here is the count, the two ways it happens, and the ledger that fixes it without inventing dates you cannot defend. What I actually collected For each domain I fetched the root sitemap.xml , followed child sitemaps one level deep, and parsed every <url> block for its <loc> and <lastmod> . No page crawling yet — this is purely what the site tells a crawler before it fetches anything. 114 domains, 30,353 URLs: 36 domains ship no lastmod at all — 9,718 URLs.

articles.title: A repair manual that has to know what is broken
articles.excerpt: A repair manual that has to know what is broken Most "how to fix X" content is a list of steps. It assumes you already know what the fault is. That assumption is where most home repairs actually fail:…
articles.body: A repair manual that has to know what is broken Most "how to fix X" content is a list of steps. It assumes you already know what the fault is. That assumption is where most home repairs actually fail: someone watches a video about replacing a fill valve when the real problem is the flapper, and buys the wrong part. So the design question I started from was not "how do I write instructions" but "how do I get from symptom to part without a technician". That changes the shape of everything. The unit is a machine, not an article Each guide opens with an animated diagram of the thing the user already owns — a tap, a toilet, a drain. The parts move because the mechanism is the explanation.

articles.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
articles.excerpt: Certain configurations of Alpine are affected. Other distros may be as well.
articles.body: Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password. The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations.

articles.excerpt: Spacewalkers Anil Menon and Joshua Kutryk installed the final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array on Thursday (Nov. 5), wrapping up a multiyear effort to boost the station's power generation by 30%.
articles.body: Just as NASA is preparing to demonstrate " Max Power " on the ground, two astronauts on a spacewalk have provided the International Space Station (ISS) with the same. Expedition 75 flight engineers Anil Menon of NASA and Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency installed and deployed the eighth and final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) on Thursday (Nov. 5), augmenting the space station's legacy solar array wings to produce as much as 30% more electricity. "We got it done!" said Menon at the end of the 6-hour-and-59-minute spacewalk . The EVA (extravehicular activity) began at 8:36 a.m. EST and ended at 3:35 p.m. EST (1336 to 2035 GMT).

articles.title: Blue Origin announces 3rd stage for its powerful New Glenn rocket —and a new engine
articles.excerpt: Blue Origin has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the launcher even more flexible and capable. The company has also built a new engine, called Northstar.
articles.body: Blue Origin's big rocket is getting a little bigger. Jeff Bezos' company announced today (Nov. 5) that it has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the powerful launcher more capable and flexible. The stage, called the GS3, "enhances New Glenn's capabilities," Blue Origin said in a blog post today . "The third stage enables direct deployment of satellite constellations to GEO [ geostationary orbit ] and supports heavy-lift science and exploration missions to the moon and deep space." Illustration of the variants of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, with the new GS3 third stage now in the mix. (Image credit: Blue Origin) New Glenn is a two-stage vehicle at the moment.

articles.body: Blue Origin CEO reportedly sent a memo to staff about the new timeline. | Anadolu via Getty Images Blue Origin plans to do its next New Glenn rocket launch in January 2027, according to CNBC and the Financial Times , which cite a memo from CEO Dave Limp sent to staff. In October, Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos told Fox News that the company was aiming for a December New Glenn launch, joking that it could be "probably December 31st." articles.title: Earth has captured a new mini moon  — but it won't stick around for long
articles.excerpt: Earth has caught itself a new mini-moon, and QQ8 is sticking around for Christmas.
articles.body: Earth has caught itself a new mini-moon, and it is sticking around for Christmas. The space rock, designated 2026 QQ8, was first observed in August 2026 after entering orbit around Earth in April 2026. The discovery was reported by the International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center on Thursday (Oct. 29). The stay of QQ8 is a temporary one. The mini-moon will remain in the thrall of Earth's gravity through December before breaking away in 2027. Scientists have recreated the orbital path of QQ8, finding that it takes 359 days, or about 0.98 of an Earth year, to orbit the sun . QQ8 closely approaches Earth around once every ten years, but this time the object came so close that Earth has been able to gravitationally seize it.
